evidence.source: 常用漢字二百字探源（金真姬）
evidence.text: The study lists 要 in Shang oracle-bone examples, including 合集8175, and in Western Zhou bronze examples, including 是要簋 and 伯要敦; it also lists Spring and Autumn, Warring States, Qin, and Han-period forms. Its analysis describes the oracle graph as 女 with two hands and a head-like upper element, and reports competing component analyses: Li Xiaoding rejects 交 as phonetic and reads the graph as a woman holding her waist; another cited proposal treats it as a compound involving 臼/女. The author concludes 要 is the original graph for 腰, with 肉 later added to distinguish the body-part word. These are scholarly interpretations, not a visually inspected glyph in this research.
evidence.title: 常用漢字二百字探源

evidence.field: 説文解字 entry for 要 (reported quotation)
evidence.text: The dossier's quotation of the Han dictionary says 要 means the middle of the body, depicts a person holding their waist, and analyzes the graph as 从𦥑 with 交省 as phonetic. The modern paleographic study above presents this as the historical Shuowen account, not as settled confirmation of the graphic analysis. The opened shuowen.org URL resolved to a different character entry, so it was not used to verify the text independently.
evidence.kind: historical dictionary account via dossier; access limitation stated
evidence.title: 說文解字「䅵」

evidence.field: graphic history and Old Chinese comparisons
evidence.text: The entry reproduces Western Zhou bronze and small-seal forms and identifies 𡢗 and 𡚩 as alternative forms. It gives a pictographic interpretation involving a person, hands, and the waist, but that specific reading is an account rather than independent paleographic proof. It lists Zhengzhang 2003 *qew for 要 and 腰 and Baxter–Sagart 2014 for 要: Middle Chinese ‹ʔjiewᴴ›, Old Chinese *[q]ew(k)-s, glossed “important.” These B–S values agree with the supplied local 要 row; that row is explicitly the MC/Tone-H form and is not interchangeable with the level-tone reading or the Zhengzhang system.
evidence.title: 要 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.text: This entry cites Guo Yongbing, “談古文字中的‘要’字和從‘要’之字,” 古文字研究 28 (2010), pp. 108–115. It reports the waist pictograph and subsequent loan analysis, while explicitly rejecting both the Shuowen 从𦥑/交省 analysis and a modern 覀+女会意 analysis. It describes senses including pivot/essential point and necessity. This records a competing scholarly interpretation; the full cited article was not inspected here.
evidence.kind: secondary lexicographic synthesis citing paleographic scholarship
evidence.title: 要 - ウィクショナリー日本語版

evidence.source: 中央研究院漢語多功能字庫
evidence.text: The database lists oracle-bone example 合集681正 and bronze example 集成09366 for 女, and explains the graph as depicting a kneeling woman with hands folded. This is relevant to 女 as a graph in general, but does not establish that 女 is a semantic or phonetic component in 要; the 要 analyses in the sources consulted instead treat the woman-like form as part of a whole-body depiction or dispute its parsing.
evidence.title: 漢字「女」：字形演變

evidence.source: 常用漢字二百字探源（金真姬）
evidence.text: The study distinguishes graphic history from word use: it cites 墨子·兼愛中 “昔者楚靈王好士細要,” 楚辭·離騷 “戶服艾以盈要兮,” and 荀子·禮論 “量要而帶之” as uses of 要 for the waist, with later commentators explicitly equating 要 and 腰. It also gives inscription records for the graph, but the excerpts inspected do not establish the date of the earliest attested waist-word use. Its account supports waist use in transmitted pre-imperial texts, not a precisely dated first occurrence.
evidence.kind: secondary scholarly study quoting transmitted texts
evidence.title: 常用漢字二百字探源

evidence.field: modern senses and proposed semantic pathway
evidence.text: The page gives current Mandarin 要 yào and discusses want, need/obligation, imminent future, and important uses. It proposes an intuitive pathway from waist as bodily pivot to essential, needed, and wanted. This is a modern pedagogical explanation, not evidence that these semantic transitions occurred in that chronological order. The inspected page supplies no dated historical examples for the want/need senses.
evidence.kind: modern pedagogical account; semantic chronology unverified
evidence.title: yao (要) — to want, must, essential in Chinese

gaps: The primary cited 2010 article by 郭永秉 was not accessed; the conflicting graph analyses are recorded through a secondary source and a separate paleographic study.

No independently verified oracle-bone or bronze occurrence for the word sense “want/need” was found. Do not infer its chronology from a modern gloss list; the textual citations inspected substantiate waist meaning only.
The exact date and semantic pathway from waist to pivot/essential, necessity, desire, obligation, and future use remain unestablished in the inspected sources.

The graph's upper and hand-like elements are disputed. No glyph image was visually inspected in this research; do not assert details such as an eye, horn, or hands shifting upward as established graphic chronology.

The source for the presumed borrowing relationship between the waist word written 要 and other 要 senses was not inspected in full. Evidence supports an established lexicographic proposal, not a demonstrated dated borrowing event.

The codepoint-specific Unicode Unihan records for 要 and 腰 failed to load. The local exact 要 rows were checked as supplied, but an official character-page click-through was not verified; no local row was used as external proof.
